verdicts.factCheck: Fetched the hl-archive-node reth fork at commit 14509628 (crates/engine/tree/src/tree/payload_validator.rs). Line 562 and line 626 assign state_root = B256::ZERO, and lines 565 and 627 compare that zero with block.header().state_root(), so the comparison passes whenever the header root is zero. Fetched nanoreth f0cad31 src/node/consensus/reth_copy.rs: it checks gas used (lines 27-34) and the receipts root and logs bloom (lines 40-51, 71-114) and nothing about state. src/node/consensus/mod.rs: validate_block_pre_execution returns Ok with all checks commented out (lines 119-147) and validate_block_post_execution calls reth_copy (lines 156-167). Fetched hyper-evm-sync main src/run.rs: assert_eq on system transaction receipts at line 236 and on all receipts at line 264; blake3_hash_slow at line 298 is only printed and stored in state_hash, not compared. On chain: eth_getBlockByNumber 0x31a0000 on https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm and https://rpc.purroofgroup.com both return hash 0xada2353e...f414, stateRoot 0x00..00 and receiptsRoot 0x64b2b701...9691. web3_clientVersion on rpc.purroofgroup.com returns reth/v0.1.0-f0cad31/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu. I re-traced the reverted-frame transaction 0xb4d698a0... (block 49,336,714) myself with callTracer withLog on nanoreth against the official receipt: status 1 on both, 8 logs in the receipt and 8 logs from non-reverted frames of the trace, equal as a multiset; the trace shows two reverted unlock frames (each with swap, take, sync, settle) and completed unlock frames around them. The raw summary hyper.json reports 2,762 traced, 0 errors, 0 status and 0 log mismatches, 258 post and 227 pre slots with 0 mismatches.
verdicts.codeCheck: src/PoolManager.sol:104-114 sets the transient unlock flag, calls the callback and reverts with CurrencyNotSettled if NonzeroDeltaCount is not zero. src/libraries/Lock.sol:10-27 and src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:18-40 use tstore and tload only. Pool state, positions, ERC-6909 balances and protocol fees are persistent storage, which is what a state root would commit to. No code path in src/ reads a block header field or the state root, so the missing state check changes no computation in src/; it only means a faulty validator write to persistent storage would not be caught by a public client until a later receipt differs. Nothing an ordinary account sends can cause such a write.
verdicts.corrections: The mechanism lists the transient storage libraries (Lock.sol, CurrencyReserves.sol, CurrencyDelta.sol, NonzeroDeltaCount.sol) among the storage that a state root check would cover. Transient storage is cleared at the end of each transaction and is never committed to any state root, so a missing state root check has no bearing on it; a validator fault in transient semantics would show in the same transaction's receipt or not at all. The relevant slots are the persistent ones in Pool, Position and the ERC-6909 and protocol fee mappings. Line numbers for the two comparisons are 565 and 627 in payload_validator.rs; 562 and 626 are the assignments. Actor operator and severity info are correct.
